one_line_contribution: Rather than transferring prompts, skeletons, or reflection heuristics across tasks, transfer a hierarchical prior over the *nuisance statistics of the search itself* — rho, the base rate at which a reflection-proposed edit is a true improvement, and the effect-size distribution of those improvements — and use it as the starting belief of a spike-and-slab sequential accept/reject test that replaces GEPA's fixed-size minibatch candidate evaluation, leaving proposal and selection untouched.
closest_prior_work: Two bodies of work jointly enclose the contribution. (1) Adaptive evaluation allocation for prompt selection is already established: TRIPLE (Shi et al., 'Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification', NeurIPS 2024) casts prompt evaluation under a fixed budget as best-arm identification and gets exactly the 'stop wasting rollouts on doomed candidates' win the proposal's mechanism (5a) claims as its own; the proposal's Related Work cites racing/SH/Hyperband generically but never engages BAI-for-prompts, which is the nearest neighbour in its own subfield. (2) Injecting an *informative, transferred* prior into a racing/allocation procedure is the core of prior-informed and meta-learned HPO: piBO (Hvarfner et al., ICLR 2022), BOPrO (Souza et al., 2021), PriorBand (Mallik et al., NeurIPS 2023) — which is precisely successive-halving-with-a-prior — and transfer surrogates such as RGPE (Feurer et al.). The proposal pre-empts this by saying transfer BO 'requires a shared, low-dimensional, parametric search space,' but that is a rebuttal to transferring a *surrogate over the search space*, not to PriorBand-style transfer of allocation beliefs, which needs no shared parameterization either. What genuinely remains is narrow: the prior is over the noise/improvement model rather than over the optimum, and it is fit hierarchically across source tasks. That is a real but modest delta, and the proposal's own baseline (iii) exists to measure exactly how thin the sliver is.
strongest_objection: Nothing in the design separates the claimed gain from 'GEPA's default minibatch size is simply too large.' Prediction (b) — 2-5 test points over cold-start GEPA at 50 rollouts, with >=60% of it traced (prediction e) to rollouts saved on rejected candidates — is the signature of spending fewer examples per candidate, which any practitioner obtains by lowering one integer. Cold-start GEPA is run only at 'its default fixed minibatch'; the ablation grid varies tau_a/tau_r, block size, and per-candidate cap for TAP but never sweeps the competitor's single most important allocation hyperparameter. A reviewer will read arm (i) as a strawman and ask what survives against GEPA with minibatch tuned once on the source tasks — a transfer of one scalar with no hierarchy, no spike-and-slab, and no sequential test. Second, the variance argument that licenses the whole statistical plan is overstated: 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed identically across evaluation-policy conditions' is impossible past the first accept/reject decision in GEPA, because the parent chosen for the next mutation depends on which candidates entered the Pareto pool. The qualifier 'where possible' quietly concedes this. Without a genuinely paired proposal stream, the effective per-comparison SD reverts toward the measured per-run ~3 points, and the '1.5-point paired difference at 80% power with n=30' calculation — the design's answer to the brief's failure mode #2 — is not supported. Third, rho is treated as a task-level constant, but it is manifestly non-stationary within a run (edits to a weak initial prompt succeed far more often than edits near convergence) and also depends on the reflector model and parent quality. Experiment 2 reports between-task vs within-task (across-seed) ICC and never conditions on iteration index, so the study can find 'rho transfers across tasks' while the real structure is 'rho is a decreasing function of optimization stage' — under which the online-prior baseline (iv), which sees the current stage, should dominate TAP everywhere except the first few candidates.
what_would_fix_it: (a) Add the minibatch/stop-rule sweep for cold-start GEPA and MIPROv2, and report TAP against the best-tuned competitor, not the default one; if TAP's advantage is only over an untuned baseline, say so and reframe the paper as a measurement paper. (b) Add a source-free generic prior arm (see missing_baseline) so 'transfer' is isolated from 'having any informative prior at all.' (c) Drop or heavily qualify the 'strictly paired design that removes proposal randomness' claim, state explicitly at which candidate index the streams must diverge, and redo the power calculation using the empirically measured paired correlation from the step-1 seed-replicate runs rather than an assumed one; alternatively run a genuinely paired sub-study in which the candidate sequence is frozen offline and only the allocation policy varies, and report that as the mechanism experiment while the full runs carry the end-to-end claim. (d) Model rho as stage-dependent (e.g., rho indexed by iteration or by parent validation score) and report the ICC decomposition with iteration as a third variance component; a hierarchical prior that pools across tasks but ignores within-run drift is the wrong object if drift dominates. (e) Resolve the internal inconsistency between 'Pareto selection exactly as is' and an accept test on aggregate P(delta>0): GEPA accepts on per-instance Pareto dominance, so the proposed test changes the selection semantics, not just the budget allocation. (f) Cut scope to fit the brief's stated ceiling of a few dozen optimization runs (see feasibility), and pre-register which of experiments 5-7 are contingent on the main result. (g) Do the preprint search and write the collision check.
missing_baseline: Two, either of which could erase the contribution. First and most damaging: cold-start GEPA/MIPROv2 with the minibatch size and promotion rule tuned on the source tasks and carried over — a 'transfer one integer' baseline that requires none of TAP's machinery and directly targets mechanism (5a). Second: a source-free generic prior — a hand-set rho (say 0.25) and a generic slab plugged into the identical sequential test, with no hierarchical fitting and no source runs at all. The proposal names this outcome in Risk Factor (1) as the scenario where 'the contribution becomes use a sensible fixed prior,' yet never instruments it: the ablations contrast single-source vs six-source pooling but never drop source-fitting entirely, so the experiment that would trigger the paper's own stated deflation is the one arm not run. Note that the uninformative-racing baseline (iii) does not substitute — a flat prior is not the same as a well-chosen fixed prior, and it is the well-chosen fixed prior that costs nothing.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and Related Work opens with '(All citations unverified; literature search was unavailable.)' By the standard stated in the review instructions this is a substantive weakness, not a neutral: the proposal asserts a 'conceptual dissociation none of these make' about a literature it has not read, and even its anchor citations (GEPA, MIPROv2) are self-declared unverified. The exposure is high rather than theoretical, because GEPA is itself a 2025 artifact and budget-aware / adaptive-evaluation variants of reflective prompt optimizers are exactly the fast-moving corner where 2025-2026 preprints cluster; 'sample-efficient candidate evaluation for DSPy/GEPA-style optimizers' and 'meta-learned priors for LLM optimizer budget allocation' are near-certain preprint topics in that window. I cannot from memory name a preprint that makes this exact claim (transferring the noise model rather than the artifact), and I am not able to search here — but the already-published TRIPLE (NeurIPS 2024) covers the adaptive-allocation half and PriorBand (NeurIPS 2023) covers the informative-prior-into-racing half, so the burden is entirely on the authors to show the intersection is open. A resubmission must include a dated search over arXiv cs.CL/cs.LG for the last ~6 months on 'prompt optimization budget allocation', 'GEPA sample efficiency', 'best-arm identification prompt', and 'transfer prior racing', with the queries and dates reported.
